title: MemeAtlas spatio-temporal event
description: One row = one event extracted from a single KYM entry's origin/spread narrative. Sub-happenings known only by relative order, with no absolute date anchor, are merged into one row rather than split into several undated rows.

frame_url.description: The KYM entry this event was extracted from — becomes the back-edge to the existing frame node when RDF-ified.

source_section.description: Which narrative section this event came from.

source_text.description: Verbatim short quote or span the event was extracted from. Provenance — lets a wrong extraction be traced back to the exact source text later.

summary.description: One or two sentences describing what happened. May cover several sub-happenings when they're only known by relative order and were merged into this one event.

date.description: Normalized date at the stated precision: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM, or YYYY. Null when date_precision is 'none'.

date_precision.description: How precise the extracted date is. 'none' covers both genuinely undated content and relative-order-only content that got merged into this row.

date_text.description: The original phrase the date was read from (e.g. 'early 2013', 'shortly after the video went viral'), kept alongside the normalized date since normalizing can lose nuance the phrase carried.

location.description: Where the event happened — a geographic place, a platform (Reddit, TikTok, 4chan), or both. Free text; null if nothing extractable.

location_type.description: Coarse tag for what kind of value 'location' holds. Optional but cheap — lets downstream RDF mapping choose the right treatment without re-parsing the string.

certainty.description: How certain this event is, per the source text's own hedging — a rumor stays a rumor in the graph rather than being flattened to fact.
